items.title: Who takes the knowledge exam
items.simple: You take the knowledge exam on a computer. You can skip it only if you have a valid license from one of these places: another U.S. state, Canada, Germany, France or the Republic of Korea.
items.official: You will need to take the knowledge exam if you do not hold a valid driver's license from another U.S. state, Canada, Germany, France, or the Republic of Korea. The two-part knowledge exam is given on a computer. Exam questions are taken from information in this manual.

items.title: Under 18: wait 15 days
items.simple: If you are under 18 and fail the knowledge exam, you must wait 15 full days to try again. For example, if you fail on January 1, your earliest retake is January 17.
items.official: If you fail the exam and you are under age 18, by law you must wait a full 15 days before you can retake the exam. For example, if you fail the exam on January 1, the earliest you can take the exam again is January 17.
items.mnemonic: Under 18? Fail, then wait 15. Fail on the 1st, retry on the 17th.

items.title: One try per business day
items.simple: You can take the knowledge exam only once per business day. You can take the road skills test only once per business day too.
items.official: The exam may be taken only once per business day. [Road skills test:] The test may be taken only once per business day.
items.mnemonic: One day, one try.

items.title: Audio, languages, no translators
items.simple: An audio version of the exam is available. The exam is offered in many languages and American Sign Language. So you may not use a translator for those languages. If you need special help, tell a DMV staff member.
items.official: An audio version of the exam is available and the exam is offered in many different languages and American Sign Language. Therefore, translators may not be used for tests in offered languages. Customers with special needs or who require special help with applications or testing should tell a DMV staff member at any DMV location.

items.title: Three fails: classroom driver ed
items.simple: If you fail the knowledge exam three times, you cannot take it a fourth time until you finish and pass the classroom part of driver education.
items.official: If you fail the knowledge exam three times, you will not be able to take it a fourth time until you complete and pass the classroom component of driver education.
items.mnemonic: Three strikes, back to class.

items.title: The 8-hour manual course
items.simple: After you fail three times, you may be able to take an 8-hour course based on this manual. Take it at a driving school or online after your third failure. If you are under 18, finish classroom driver education first.
items.official: You may have the option of completing an 8-hour course based on the Virginia Driver's Manual and approved by DMV exclusively for satisfying the three-times-failure requirement. This course is available at a driver training school and online. Customers younger than 18 may complete the course if they have previously completed the classroom component of driver education. The completion date must be after the date that you failed the knowledge exam the third time.
items.mnemonic: Three fails? Eight hours.

items.title: Exam rules: no help, no phone
items.simple: During the exam, you cannot get help or help someone else. You cannot get or give test questions or answers. You cannot use a cell phone.
items.official: When testing, you cannot: get help while taking the exam; help another person taking the exam; try to get test questions or answers before the exam; give another person exam questions or answers; use a cell phone during the exam.
items.mnemonic: Just you and the screen. No help, no phone.

items.title: Who takes the road test
items.simple: You must take the road skills test. You can skip it only if you have a valid license from one of these places: another U.S. state, Canada, Germany, France, the Republic of Korea or Taiwan.
items.official: You will need to take the road skills test if you do not hold a valid driver's license from another U.S. state, Canada, Germany, France, the Republic of Korea, or Taiwan.
items.mnemonic: Road test skip list = exam skip list + Taiwan.

items.title: Road test: bring a safe car
items.simple: You must provide the car for the road test. It cannot be an autocycle. It needs a valid inspection sticker, plates and registration. The brakes, seat belts, horn, lights, turn signals, mirrors and speedometer must all work.
items.official: You must provide a vehicle for the road skills test (cannot be taken in an autocycle). The vehicle must have a valid safety inspection sticker, license plates, registration card and decals, working brakes, safety belts, horn, lights, turn signals, mirrors and speedometer.

items.title: Driver ed papers or checklist
items.simple: For the road test, show a driver education completion certificate, or fill out a behind-the-wheel checklist. On the checklist, a licensed driver must say they practiced with you. The driver must also say you followed all permit rules.
items.official: The DMV examiner will require that you either present an acceptable driver's education certificate of completion, or complete a behind-the-wheel checklist (DMV form CSMA 19). A licensed driver will need to certify on the form that he/she has been with you while you practiced the driving tasks and that you have complied with all requirements for learner's permit holders.

items.title: Under 18: test in driver ed
items.simple: If you are under 18, your road skills test is part of your driver education course. A public, private or commercial driving school gives the test.
items.official: For applicants under 18, the road skills test will be given as part of the driver education course taken at a public, private or commercial driving school.

items.title: 18+: 60-day permit or driver ed
items.simple: If you are 18 or older, you must hold your learner's permit for 60 days before your first road test, or finish driver ed at an approved school. With driver ed, the school tests you. With the permit, DMV does.
items.official: Applicants age 18 or older must hold the learner's permit for 60 days prior to the first road skills test or complete a course of driver's education at a driver training school approved by DMV or the Department of Education. For applicants who choose driver's education, the road skills test will be administered by the driver training school. For those who opt to hold a learner's permit for 60 days, the road skills test will be given by a DMV staff member.
items.mnemonic: 18 and up: 60 days or driver ed.

items.title: Failed road test: wait 2 days
items.simple: If you fail the road skills test, you must wait two days to try again. If you fail it at DMV three times, you must first pass the in-car part of driver ed.
items.official: If you fail the road skills test, you must wait two days to take it again. If you fail the road skills test at DMV three times, you will not be able to take it a fourth time until you complete and pass the in-vehicle part of driver education at a driver training school approved by DMV or the Department of Education.
items.mnemonic: Road test fail: wait 2. Exam fail under 18: wait 15.

items.title: Vision screening for everyone
items.simple: Your tests always include a vision screening. You look into a machine and read letters or numbers. It is not a medical exam. If you fail the screening, you may need to see an eye care professional.
items.official: Tests will include a vision screening and may include a two-part knowledge exam and a road skills test. A DMV representative will tell you which tests you need to take. A DMV staff member will ask you to look into a machine and read a series of letters or numbers. The vision screening is not a medical exam. If you fail the vision screening, you may be asked to visit an eye care professional.

items.title: Restriction C: wear your glasses
items.simple: If you need glasses or contacts to pass the vision screening, you must wear them every time you drive. Your license shows the letter C for this restriction.
items.official: If you need to wear glasses or contact lenses to pass the vision screening, you must wear them when you drive. Your license will display a C for this restriction. To have this restriction removed after having laser surgery to correct your vision, you must visit a DMV customer service center and pass the vision screening without wearing glasses or contact lenses or submit a Vision Screening Report (MED 4).
items.mnemonic: C on your card? Glasses on your face.

items.title: No limits: 20/40 and 110
items.simple: To get a license with no vision limits, you need 20/40 vision or better in one or both eyes. You also need 110 degrees or more of side vision.
items.official: Driver's license - unrestricted: 20/40 or better vision in one or both eyes, and 110 degrees, or better, horizontal vision in one or both eyes.
items.mnemonic: Full license: 20/40 and 110.

items.title: Daylight only: 20/70 and 70
items.simple: A daylight-only license needs 20/70 vision or better. You also need 70 degrees or more of side vision. If only one eye sees, you need 30 degrees of side vision toward your nose and 40 degrees toward your temple.
items.official: Driving - restricted to daylight hours only: 20/70 or better vision in one or both eyes, and 70 degrees, or better, horizontal vision. If you have vision in only one eye, you must have horizontal vision of at least 30 degrees or better when looking toward your nose and 40 degrees or better when looking toward your temple.
items.mnemonic: 70 and 70: daylight only. One eye: nose 30, temple 40. Numbers grow as you look out.

items.title: Daylight hours: half-hour rule
items.simple: If you have a daylight-only license, you may begin driving a half hour after sunrise. You must stop driving a half hour before sunset. Never drive outside those times.
items.official: A daylight driving only restricted license permits you to drive only during the period of time beginning a half-hour after sunrise and ending a half-hour before sunset.
items.mnemonic: Sunrise plus a half hour. Sunset minus a half hour.

items.title: Always carry your license
items.simple: Whenever you drive, carry your valid driver's license or learner's permit with you. Misusing your license or permit is illegal. You could pay a fine, go to jail, or lose your license.
items.official: Whenever you drive, you must carry a valid driver's license or learner's permit with you. Any misuse of your driver's license or learner's permit is illegal. You could be fined, sentenced to jail, or your license may be suspended.

items.title: Permit: who rides with you
items.simple: With a learner's permit, a licensed driver aged 21 or older must sit in the front passenger seat. A licensed driver aged 18 to 20 may sit there only if that person is your brother, sister or legal guardian.
items.official: A learner's permit allows you to operate a motor vehicle when a licensed driver at least 21 years of age is seated in the front passenger seat. The driver with you must hold a valid driver's license, be alert and able to assist you while you are driving. The licensed driver with you may be age 18, 19, or 20 if he or she is your legal guardian, brother, sister, half-brother, half-sister, step brother or stepsister.
items.mnemonic: Permit pal: 21 up, or a sibling or guardian 18 up.

items.title: Age 19+: permit 60 days
items.simple: If you are 19 or older, you must hold your learner's permit for 60 days before you apply for a license. You can show a driver ed completion certificate instead.
items.official: If you are age 19 or older, you must hold a learner's permit for 60 days, or present a driver's education certificate of completion to apply for a driver's license.
items.mnemonic: 19 and up: 60 days or a certificate.

items.title: Regular license: under 26,001 lbs
items.simple: A regular driver's license lets you drive cars. It also covers small trucks under 26,001 pounds. The truck must be one that does not need a CDL.
items.official: A driver's license allows you to operate any vehicle or small truck less than 26,001 pounds that is exempt from commercial driver's license (CDL) requirements.

items.title: CDL for big vehicles
items.simple: Big vehicles need a commercial driver's license (CDL). These include tractor-trailers, passenger buses, tank vehicles and vehicles that carry hazardous materials. A school bus for 16 or more people needs one too. Count the driver as one of them.
items.official: A commercial driver's license (CDL) allows you to operate tractor-trailers, passenger buses, tank vehicles, school buses for 16 or more occupants (including the driver), or vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

items.title: 15-person school bus endorsement
items.simple: A school bus built for 15 people, counting the driver, does not need a CDL. But you must pass the commercial driver test and the school bus test. Then you get a school bus endorsement on your license.
items.official: If you wish to operate a school bus designed to carry 15 occupants (including the driver), you do not need to obtain a commercial driver's license. However, you will need to take the commercial driver and school bus tests to obtain the school bus endorsement on your driver's license. You will be restricted to driving a bus designed to carry 15 occupants (including the driver).
items.mnemonic: 15 people: endorsement. 16 or more: CDL.

items.title: International license is not a license
items.simple: An international driver's license is not a real license. It does not let you drive. It is only a translation of your real license for travel outside the U.S.
items.official: An international driver's license is not a valid driver's license and does not allow you to drive. It is only a foreign translation of your existing valid driver's license to be used when you are traveling outside of the U.S. These permits are issued by your local AAA, except to persons whose driving privilege is suspended or revoked. If you are visiting the U.S. from a foreign country, you may drive using your driver's license issued by your home country, accompanied by a translation. International driver's licenses marketed by private sector businesses are not valid. Sale of any document claiming to be a driver's license is a Class 1 misdemeanor.

items.title: License by mail; move in 30
items.simple: Your new license comes in the mail, not at the DMV office. If you move, tell DMV within 30 days. The post office will not forward your license.
items.official: You will receive your new driver's license in the mail. For security, DMV does not issue licenses in customer service centers. If you move, you are required to notify DMV within 30 days. The postal service will not forward your license to another address. If DMV does not have your correct address, the postal service will return the license to DMV.
items.mnemonic: Move? Tell DMV in 30.

items.title: New resident: license in 60 days
items.simple: If you move to Virginia and drive, you must get a Virginia driver's license within 60 days of moving.
items.official: If you are a new Virginia resident and drive, you must obtain a Virginia driver's license within 60 days of moving here.
items.mnemonic: New here: plates in 30, license in 60.

items.title: Title, register, plates: 30 days
items.simple: If you move to Virginia, you must title and register your vehicle and get Virginia license plates within 30 days of moving. Your city or county may also require you to register it there.
items.official: Title and register your vehicle and obtain Virginia license plates within 30 days of moving to Virginia. You must also register your vehicle in your locality, if required. Check with your city or county government.
items.mnemonic: New here: plates in 30, license in 60.

items.title: Two plates and the card
items.simple: Put license plates on the front and back of your car. Put the registration decals on the plates. They show the month and year when your registration ends. Keep your registration card with you when you drive.
items.official: License plates must be displayed on the front and rear of the vehicle. Decals indicating the month and year that the registration expires must be placed in the designated areas on the plates (except for vehicles displaying permanent plates). You must have the vehicle registration card with you when operating the vehicle.
items.mnemonic: Plates front and back. Card in the car.

items.title: Safety inspection every year
items.simple: Your vehicle must pass a safety inspection every year. It must show a valid inspection sticker. Some places also require an emissions inspection.
items.official: Your vehicle must pass an annual vehicle safety inspection and display a valid safety inspection sticker. In certain localities, your vehicle also must pass an emissions inspection.

items.title: The penny tread test
items.simple: Use a penny to check your tires every month or before a long trip. Put Lincoln's head into a tread groove. If the tread covers part of his head, your tread is safe.
items.official: Once every month, or before a long road trip, check your tires for wear and damage problems by using the penny test. Select a point on your tire where the tread appears to be lowest and place Lincoln's head into one of the grooves. If any part of Lincoln's head is covered by the tread, you're driving with the safe amount of tread. If your tread gets below that, your car's ability to grip the road in adverse conditions is greatly reduced.
items.mnemonic: Lincoln's head hidden a bit? Tread is fit.

items.title: Tire pressure: check the door jamb
items.simple: Before you get in the car, check your tire pressure with a tire pressure gauge. The right PSI is in your owner's manual or on the driver's side door jamb.
items.official: Prior to entering the vehicle, check tire pressure using a tire pressure gauge. The recommended PSI (pounds per square inch) is located in the vehicle owner's manual or the driver's side door jamb of the vehicle.
items.mnemonic: Penny for tread. Gauge for air.

items.title: Register to vote at DMV
items.simple: You can apply to register to vote at any DMV office. You can also change your voter address there. You must be a U.S. citizen and live in Virginia. You must be 18 by the next general election.
items.official: You may apply to register to vote or to change your voter registration mailing address at any DMV office. To apply to register to vote in Virginia, you must be a U.S. citizen, a resident of Virginia, and be at least 18 years old by the next general election. You must have had your voting rights restored by a circuit court if you have been convicted of a felony or if you have been declared mentally incompetent.

items.title: Organ donor: check yes
items.simple: To become an organ, eye and tissue donor, check yes on your license, permit or ID card application. If you are under 18 years old, your parents or guardians make the final decision.
items.official: To sign up to be a donor, check yes on your driver's license, learners permit, or ID card application. If you are age 18 or older, your registered decision to be a donor will be honored. If you are under age 18, you can indicate your wishes to donate by checking yes; by law, your parents and guardians must make the final decision.

events.prompt: What does Restriction C on your license require?
events.missLine: Restriction C means you must wear your glasses or contact lenses when you drive.

events.prompt: If you need glasses to pass the DMV vision screening, what must you do?
events.missLine: If you need glasses or contacts to pass the vision screening, you must wear them every time you drive.

events.prompt: What is the worst vision allowed for an unrestricted license?
events.missLine: An unrestricted license needs 20/40 vision or better.

events.prompt: What is the least side vision allowed for an unrestricted license?
events.missLine: An unrestricted license needs 110 degrees or more of horizontal vision.

events.prompt: With 20/40 vision and 110 degrees of side vision, which license do you qualify for?
events.missLine: You qualify for an unrestricted license with 20/40 vision and 110 degrees of side vision.

events.prompt: What is the worst vision allowed for a daylight-only license?
events.missLine: A daylight-only license needs 20/70 vision or better.

events.prompt: What is the least side vision allowed for a daylight-only license?
events.missLine: A daylight-only license needs 70 degrees or more of horizontal vision.

events.prompt: With 20/70 vision and 70 degrees of side vision, which license do you qualify for?
events.missLine: You qualify for a daylight-only license with 20/70 vision and 70 degrees of side vision.

events.missLine: With a daylight-only license, you may drive only from a half hour after sunrise to a half hour before sunset.

events.prompt: With a daylight-only license, what is the earliest time you may drive?
events.missLine: With a daylight-only license, you may start driving a half hour after sunrise.

events.prompt: With a daylight-only license, when must you stop driving?
events.missLine: With a daylight-only license, you must stop driving a half hour before sunset.

events.prompt: Your license is daylight-only. It is a sunny noon, and the light is green.
events.missLine: Noon is inside daylight hours, so a green light means go.

events.prompt: You are heading out to drive. You left your license inside!

events.prompt: When must you carry your license?

events.prompt: What can happen if you misuse your license?
events.missLine: Misusing a license or permit can bring a fine, jail or suspension.

events.prompt: At a minimum, how old must your permit supervisor be?

events.missLine: The licensed driver with you must sit in the front passenger seat.

events.prompt: Can your licensed 19-year-old sister supervise you on a learner's permit?

events.prompt: A regular license covers trucks under how many pounds?

events.prompt: Which license covers a truck under 26,001 pounds that does not need a CDL?

events.prompt: Which license do you need to drive a tractor-trailer?
events.missLine: Tractor-trailers need a commercial driver's license (CDL).

events.prompt: Which license do you need to drive a school bus for 16 or more people?

events.prompt: How soon must you tell DMV after you move?

events.prompt: Will the post office forward your license to your new address?

events.prompt: How soon must a new Virginia resident who drives get a Virginia license?

events.prompt: How soon after moving to Virginia must you title your vehicle and get license plates?

events.missLine: Keep the vehicle registration card with you whenever you drive.

events.prompt: What do the decals on your license plate show?
events.missLine: Plate decals show the month and year your registration expires.

events.prompt: You left your registration card at home!
events.missLine: Keep your registration card with you whenever you drive.

events.prompt: How often must your car pass a safety inspection?
events.missLine: Your vehicle must pass a safety inspection every year.

events.prompt: Besides a safety inspection, which inspection do some localities require?
events.missLine: In certain localities, your vehicle must also pass an emissions inspection.

events.prompt: Your car's inspection sticker has expired!
events.missLine: Your vehicle must pass a safety inspection every year and show a valid inspection sticker.

events.prompt: How often should you do the penny test on your tires?
events.missLine: Do the penny test once a month, or before a long road trip.

events.prompt: In the penny test, what does it mean if the tread covers part of Lincoln's head?
choices: Your tires have too much air
events.missLine: If the tread covers any part of Lincoln's head, your tread is safe.

events.prompt: Where on the tire should you put the penny?
events.missLine: Put the penny where the tread looks lowest.

events.prompt: Where can you find the right PSI for your tires?
events.missLine: Find the recommended PSI in the owner's manual or on the driver's side door jamb.

events.prompt: What tool do you use to check tire pressure?
events.missLine: Use a tire pressure gauge. The penny test is for tread.

events.prompt: When should you check your tire pressure?
choices: Before you get in the car
events.missLine: Check your tire pressure before you get into the vehicle.

events.prompt: Can you apply to register to vote at a DMV office?
choices: Yes, but only on election day
events.missLine: You may apply to register to vote at any DMV office.

events.prompt: When must you be 18 to register to vote?
events.missLine: You must be at least 18 by the next general election.

events.prompt: How do you sign up to be an organ donor in Virginia?
events.missLine: Check yes on your license, permit, or ID card application.

events.prompt: Who makes the final decision about being an organ donor if you are under 18?
events.missLine: If you are under 18, your parents or guardians make the final decision about being an organ donor.

questions.prompt: How is the Virginia knowledge exam given?
choices: In a car, with an examiner
questions.explain: The two-part knowledge exam is given on a computer.

questions.prompt: Which valid driver's license lets a new resident skip the knowledge exam?
choices: A license from another U.S. state
questions.explain: You may skip the knowledge exam with a valid license from another U.S. state, Canada, Germany, France, or the Republic of Korea.

questions.prompt: Where do the questions on the Virginia DMV knowledge exam come from?
questions.explain: Exam questions are taken from information in the Virginia Driver's Manual.

questions.prompt: If you are under 18 and fail the DMV knowledge exam, how long must you wait to retake it?
questions.explain: By law, if you are under 18, you must wait a full 15 days to retake the exam.

questions.prompt: You are 17 and fail the DMV knowledge exam on January 1. What is the earliest date you can take it again?
questions.explain: When you are under 18, you must wait a full 15 days, so after a January 1 fail the earliest retake date is January 17.

questions.prompt: Who must wait 15 days to retake a failed DMV knowledge exam?
questions.explain: By law, people under age 18 must wait a full 15 days to retake the exam.

questions.prompt: How often may you take the DMV knowledge exam?
choices: Up to three times a day
As many times as you want in one day
questions.explain: You may take the knowledge exam only once per business day.

questions.prompt: How often may you take the DMV road skills test?
choices: Up to three times a day
questions.explain: You may take the road skills test only once per business day.

questions.prompt: Why are translators not allowed for the DMV knowledge exam?
choices: The exam is given only in English
The exam is offered in many languages and American Sign Language
questions.explain: The exam comes in many languages and American Sign Language, so translators may not be used.

questions.prompt: Which version of the DMV knowledge exam is available?
questions.explain: An audio version of the exam is available.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you need special help with DMV testing?
choices: Bring a friend to help you
questions.explain: If you need special help with testing, you should tell a DMV staff member.

questions.prompt: If you fail the DMV knowledge exam three times, what must you do before you can take it a fourth time?
choices: Complete and pass the classroom part of driver education
Hold a learner's permit for 60 days
questions.explain: After three failed exams, you must complete and pass the classroom part of driver education.

questions.prompt: After how many failed DMV knowledge exams must you pass classroom driver education before you can take the exam again?
questions.explain: After three failed knowledge exams, you must complete classroom driver education first.

questions.prompt: How long is the DMV-approved course for people who fail the knowledge exam three times?
questions.explain: The course based on the Virginia Driver's Manual is 8 hours long.

questions.prompt: What must a person under 18 do before taking the 8-hour driver's manual course?
choices: Hold a learner's permit for 60 days
Complete the classroom part of driver education
questions.explain: A person younger than 18 must have completed classroom driver education first.

questions.prompt: Which statement is true about the 8-hour driver's manual course?
choices: You must finish it before your first knowledge exam
You must finish it within 15 days of your first exam
You must finish it after the date of your third failed knowledge exam
You must finish it only at a DMV office
questions.explain: You must finish the course after the date of your third failed knowledge exam.

questions.prompt: What is not allowed while you take the DMV knowledge exam?
questions.explain: During the exam, you cannot get help, give help, or use a cell phone.

questions.prompt: Which of these is allowed when you take the DMV knowledge exam?
choices: Using the audio version of the exam
Getting exam answers before the exam
questions.explain: You may use the audio version. You may not use a phone, get answers early, or help others.

questions.prompt: What is the rule about giving another person DMV exam questions or answers?
choices: It is allowed after you finish
It is allowed if they are family
It is allowed for some questions
questions.explain: You cannot give another person exam questions or answers.

questions.prompt: Which valid driver's licenses let you skip the road skills test?
choices: Licenses from any country in North America
Licenses from another U.S. state, Canada, Germany, France, the Republic of Korea, or Taiwan
Licenses from any country in the world
Licenses only from the states that border Virginia
questions.explain: You may skip the road skills test with a valid license from another U.S. state, Canada, Germany, France, the Republic of Korea, or Taiwan.

questions.prompt: Which tests does a person getting a very first driver's license take?
choices: A vision screening, a knowledge exam, and a road skills test
questions.explain: Everyone gets a vision screening, and a first-time driver also takes the knowledge exam and the road skills test.

questions.prompt: Which valid driver's license lets you skip the road skills test but not the knowledge exam?
choices: A license from another U.S. state
questions.explain: A license from Taiwan lets you skip the road skills test. It does not let you skip the knowledge exam.

questions.prompt: What must your vehicle have for the road skills test?
questions.explain: Your vehicle needs a valid inspection sticker, plates, registration, and working equipment such as turn signals and a horn.

questions.prompt: Which vehicle can you not use for the road skills test?
choices: A car with a valid inspection sticker
questions.explain: You must provide a vehicle, and it cannot be an autocycle.

questions.prompt: Besides a driver education certificate of completion, what can you present to take the road skills test?
choices: A behind-the-wheel checklist signed by a licensed driver
questions.explain: The DMV examiner requires either a driver education certificate or a behind-the-wheel checklist.

questions.prompt: Which fact does a licensed driver certify on the behind-the-wheel checklist?
choices: The driver was with you while you practiced the driving tasks
You have never had a ticket
questions.explain: The licensed driver certifies that they were with you while you practiced and that you followed all permit rules.

questions.prompt: What is true about the road skills test for applicants under 18?
choices: It is given as part of the driver education course
It is given by a parent at home
It is given at a police station
It is given only after you turn 18
questions.explain: For applicants under 18, the road test is part of the driver education course at a public, private, or commercial driving school.

questions.prompt: Which applicants take the road skills test as part of a driver education course?
choices: Applicants with a license from Canada
questions.explain: Applicants under 18 take the road skills test as part of driver education.

questions.prompt: If you are 18 or older, what must you do before your first road skills test?
choices: Hold a learner's permit for 30 days
Hold a learner's permit for 60 days or complete driver education
questions.explain: If you are 18 or older, you must hold the permit for 60 days or complete driver education first.

questions.prompt: Who gives the road skills test to an adult who completes driver education at an approved driver training school?
questions.explain: When an adult chooses driver education, the driver training school gives the road skills test.

questions.prompt: If you are 18 or older and do not take driver education, how long must you hold a learner's permit before your first road skills test?
questions.explain: Without driver education, an applicant who is 18 or older must hold the learner's permit for 60 days.

questions.prompt: If you fail the DMV road skills test, how long must you wait to take it again?
questions.explain: If you fail the road skills test, you must wait two days to take it again.

questions.prompt: If you fail the road skills test at the DMV three times, what must you do before a fourth try?
choices: Complete and pass the in-vehicle part of driver education
questions.explain: After you fail the road skills test three times at the DMV, you must complete and pass the in-vehicle part of driver education.

questions.prompt: After three failed road skills tests at the DMV, which statement is true about the in-vehicle part of driver education?
choices: You must finish it before your first road skills test
You must finish it after the date of your third failed road skills test
You must finish it within two days of your third failure
You must finish it at a DMV customer service center
questions.explain: You must finish the in-vehicle part of driver education after the date of your third failed road skills test.

questions.prompt: What is true about the DMV vision screening?
choices: It is not a medical exam
It is a full medical exam
It is only for drivers over 65
It is only for CDL drivers
questions.explain: The vision screening is not a medical exam. It shows whether your vision meets Virginia's standards for safe driving.

questions.prompt: What will you do during the vision screening?
choices: Read a page of the manual aloud
Look into a machine and read letters or numbers
Get eye drops from a doctor
questions.explain: A DMV staff member asks you to look into a machine and read letters or numbers.

questions.prompt: What may you be asked to do if you fail the vision screening?
choices: Take the road skills test twice
questions.explain: If you fail the vision screening, you may be asked to visit an eye care professional.

questions.prompt: Who tells you which DMV tests you need to take?
questions.explain: A DMV representative tells you which tests you need to take.

questions.prompt: If you need glasses to pass the vision screening, what will your license show?
questions.explain: If you need glasses or contacts to pass, your license shows a C restriction.

questions.prompt: What must you do if your license has a C restriction?
choices: Wear your glasses or contacts when you drive
Drive only with a licensed driver age 21 or older
questions.explain: A C restriction means you must wear your glasses or contacts when you drive.

questions.prompt: What must you do to remove a glasses restriction after laser eye surgery?
choices: Pass the vision screening without glasses or contacts, or submit a Vision Screening Report
Take the road skills test again
questions.explain: After laser surgery, you must pass the screening without glasses or contacts, or submit a Vision Screening Report (MED 4).

questions.prompt: How good must your vision be to get an unrestricted driver's license?
questions.explain: An unrestricted license needs 20/40 or better vision in one or both eyes.

questions.prompt: At least how many degrees of horizontal vision do you need for an unrestricted license?
questions.explain: You need 110 degrees or more of horizontal vision for an unrestricted license.

questions.prompt: What may a driver with 20/40 vision and 110 degrees of horizontal vision get?
questions.explain: Vision of 20/40 with 110 degrees of horizontal vision meets the standard for an unrestricted license.

questions.prompt: What restriction may a driver with 20/70 vision and 70 degrees of horizontal vision get?
questions.explain: Vision of 20/70 with 70 degrees of horizontal vision meets the standard for a daylight-only license.

questions.prompt: How good must your vision be to get a license restricted to daylight driving?
questions.explain: A daylight-only license needs 20/70 or better vision in one or both eyes.

questions.prompt: If you have vision in only one eye, at least how much horizontal vision does a daylight-only license require?
choices: 40 degrees toward your nose and 30 degrees toward your temple
70 degrees toward your nose and 110 degrees toward your temple
30 degrees toward your nose and 40 degrees toward your temple
10 degrees toward your nose and 20 degrees toward your temple
questions.explain: With vision in only one eye, you need at least 30 degrees toward your nose and 40 degrees toward your temple.

questions.prompt: With a daylight-only restricted license, when may you drive?
choices: From a half hour after sunrise until a half hour before sunset
From one hour after sunrise until one hour before sunset
From a half hour before sunrise until a half hour after sunset
questions.explain: A daylight-only license lets you drive from a half hour after sunrise until a half hour before sunset.

questions.prompt: When must you stop driving with a daylight-only license?
questions.explain: With a daylight-only license, you must stop driving a half hour before sunset.

questions.prompt: What must you carry whenever you drive?
choices: A valid driver's license or learner's permit
questions.explain: You must carry a valid driver's license or learner's permit whenever you drive.

questions.prompt: What can happen if you misuse your driver's license or learner's permit?
questions.explain: Misusing your license or permit is illegal. You can be fined, sentenced to jail, or have your license suspended.

questions.prompt: How old must a licensed driver be, at least, to sit in the front passenger seat while you drive with a learner's permit?
questions.explain: The licensed driver must be at least 21. A legal guardian, brother or sister who is 18 to 20 is also allowed.

questions.prompt: When you drive with a learner's permit, what must the licensed driver with you do?
choices: Sit in the front passenger seat
Be alert and able to help you
questions.explain: The driver with you must hold a valid license, sit in the front passenger seat, and be alert and able to help you.

questions.prompt: Which licensed driver who is 18, 19 or 20 may supervise your driving with a learner's permit?
choices: Your brother, sister or legal guardian
questions.explain: A supervising driver age 18 to 20 must be your legal guardian, brother, sister, half-sibling or stepsibling.

questions.prompt: Your licensed 19-year-old stepbrother is sitting in the front passenger seat. May you drive with your learner's permit?
choices: Yes, but only in parking lots
questions.explain: A licensed stepbrother age 18 to 20 may be your supervising driver, so you may drive.

questions.prompt: If you are 19 or older, what can you do instead of holding a learner's permit for 60 days before you apply for a driver's license?
choices: Present a driver's education certificate of completion
Bring a note from a parent
questions.explain: If you are 19 or older, you must hold the permit for 60 days or show a driver's education certificate of completion.

questions.prompt: How long must a 19-year-old who has not taken driver education hold a learner's permit before applying for a license?
questions.explain: A 19-year-old without driver education must hold a learner's permit for 60 days.

questions.prompt: A regular driver's license allows you to drive a small truck that weighs less than how many pounds?
questions.explain: A driver's license covers small trucks that weigh less than 26,001 pounds and do not need a CDL.

questions.prompt: Which vehicle can you drive with a regular Virginia driver's license?
questions.explain: A regular license covers cars. Tractor-trailers, tank vehicles and hazardous materials vehicles need a CDL.

questions.prompt: For which of these vehicles do you need a commercial driver's license (CDL)?
questions.explain: You need a CDL for tractor-trailers, passenger buses, tank vehicles, big school buses and hazardous materials vehicles.

questions.prompt: How many occupants, including the driver, must a school bus carry before you need a CDL to drive it?
questions.explain: You need a CDL for a school bus that carries 16 or more occupants, including the driver.

questions.prompt: What do you need to drive a school bus designed to carry 15 occupants, including the driver?
choices: A school bus endorsement on your license
questions.explain: A school bus designed to carry 15 occupants needs a school bus endorsement, not a CDL.

questions.prompt: What must you pass to get a school bus endorsement?
choices: The commercial driver and school bus tests
questions.explain: To get the endorsement, you must take the commercial driver and school bus tests.

questions.prompt: A school bus endorsement limits you to driving a bus designed to carry how many occupants?
questions.explain: The endorsement limits you to a bus designed to carry 15 occupants, including the driver.

questions.prompt: Which statement about an international driver's license is true?
choices: It lets you drive without any other license
It is not a valid driver's license
It is issued by Virginia DMV
questions.explain: An international driver's license does not allow you to drive. It is only a translation of your real license.

questions.prompt: What can a visitor from a foreign country use to drive in the U.S.?
choices: Their home country's driver's license with a translation
An international license bought from a private business
questions.explain: A visitor may drive with a license from their home country, along with a translation.

questions.prompt: How does the law treat the sale of any document that claims to be a driver's license?
choices: It is legal if the document is sold online
questions.explain: Selling any document that claims to be a driver's license is a Class 1 misdemeanor.

questions.prompt: How will you receive your new driver's license?
choices: At the DMV customer service center that day
questions.explain: For security, DMV mails licenses. It does not issue them in customer service centers.

questions.prompt: Within how many days must you notify DMV if you move?
questions.explain: If you move, you must notify DMV within 30 days.

questions.prompt: What will happen to your new license if DMV does not have your correct address?
choices: It will be returned to DMV by the postal service
It will be forwarded to your new address
It will be left at your old address
It will be sent to your school
questions.explain: The postal service will not forward your license, so it goes back to DMV.

questions.prompt: After moving to Virginia, how long do new residents who drive have to get a Virginia driver's license?
questions.explain: New residents who drive must get a Virginia driver's license within 60 days of moving here.

questions.prompt: What must a new Virginia resident do?
choices: Get a license within 60 days, and title and register your vehicle and get plates within 30 days
Get a license within 30 days, and get plates for your vehicle within 60 days
Get a license and get plates for your vehicle within one year
Get a license and get plates for your vehicle within 10 days
questions.explain: New residents have 60 days to get a license. They have 30 days to title and register a vehicle and get plates.

questions.prompt: After you move to Virginia, how soon must you title and register your vehicle and get Virginia plates?
questions.explain: You must title and register your vehicle and get Virginia license plates within 30 days of moving to Virginia.

questions.prompt: What must you do within 30 days of moving to Virginia?
choices: Title and register your vehicle and get Virginia license plates
Sign up as an organ donor
questions.explain: New residents must title and register their vehicles and get Virginia plates within 30 days.

questions.prompt: Where must license plates be displayed on a vehicle?
choices: On the front and the rear of the vehicle
Only on the rear of the vehicle
Only on the front of the vehicle
questions.explain: Virginia license plates must be on the front and the rear of the vehicle.

questions.prompt: What must you have with you when you drive?
questions.explain: You must have the vehicle registration card with you when you drive.

questions.prompt: What do the decals on your license plates show?
choices: The month and year when the registration expires
questions.explain: The decals show the month and year when the registration expires.

questions.prompt: How often must your vehicle pass a safety inspection in Virginia?
questions.explain: Virginia requires your vehicle to pass a safety inspection every year.

questions.prompt: What must your vehicle display after it passes a safety inspection?
questions.explain: After it passes inspection, your vehicle must display a valid safety inspection sticker.

questions.prompt: In some localities, what else must your vehicle pass?
questions.explain: Some localities also require your vehicle to pass an emissions inspection.

questions.prompt: In the penny test, what does it mean if the tread covers any part of Lincoln's head?
choices: You have a safe amount of tread
Your tires need replacing right away
Your tire pressure is too low
Your tires have too much air
questions.explain: If the tread covers any part of Lincoln's head, you have a safe amount of tread.

questions.prompt: How often should you check your tires with the penny test?
choices: Once every month, or before a long road trip
Only when a tire looks flat
questions.explain: You should check your tires with the penny test once every month or before a long road trip.

questions.prompt: What happens if your tire tread gets too low?
choices: Your car grips the road much less in bad conditions
Your tires grip better in rain
questions.explain: Low tread greatly reduces your car's grip on the road in bad conditions.

questions.prompt: Where can you find the recommended tire pressure (PSI) for your vehicle?
choices: In the owner's manual or on the driver's side door jamb
questions.explain: The recommended PSI is in the owner's manual or on the driver's side door jamb.

questions.prompt: What should you use to check your tire pressure?
questions.explain: Use a tire pressure gauge to check tire pressure before you get in the vehicle.

questions.prompt: What must you be to apply to register to vote in Virginia?
choices: At least 18 years old by the next general election
questions.explain: You must be a U.S. citizen, a Virginia resident, and at least 18 years old by the next general election.

questions.prompt: When or where can you apply to register to vote or change your voter mailing address?
questions.explain: You may apply to register to vote or change your voter mailing address at any DMV office.

questions.prompt: What must you do first if you have been convicted of a felony and want to register to vote in Virginia?
choices: Have your voting rights restored by a circuit court
questions.explain: After a felony conviction, a circuit court must restore your voting rights before you can register to vote.

questions.prompt: What can you do to sign up as an organ, eye, and tissue donor?
choices: Check yes on your driver's license, permit, or ID card application
Write it on your license plate
Do nothing, because everyone is signed up
questions.explain: You can sign up to be a donor by checking yes on your license, permit, or ID card application.

questions.prompt: What happens if you are under 18 and check yes to be a donor?
choices: Your parents or guardians make the final decision
The DMV makes the final decision
Your choice does not count at all
questions.explain: By law, your parents or guardians make the final decision if you are under 18.

questions.prompt: What will happen to your registered decision to be a donor if you are 18 or older?
choices: It will be decided by your parents
It will be canceled at age 21
questions.explain: If you are 18 or older, your registered decision to be a donor will be honored.
